package_info.package_name: N/A (general web loyalty program attack patterns)
package_info.why_malicious: The report details two primary attack vectors targeting online loyalty programs: (1) credential harvesting through phishing overlays that mimic legitimate login pages, and (2) malicious JavaScript injection into actual loyalty program pages to exfiltrate sensitive customer data such as credentials, contact information, and payment details. Both methods enable unauthorized access, account takeover, and theft of personal and financial information, resulting in significant risk to users and businesses.

execution_context.trigger: When a user attempts to log in on the fake loyalty program page
execution_context.file_location: Transparent overlay mimicking the legitimate loyalty program login page (HTML/CSS/JavaScript served from attacker infrastructure)
required_permissions: read access to user input fields

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HTML/CSS/JavaScript code that visually replicates the legitimate loyalty program login interface. The JavaScript captures user-entered credentials (username, password, and potentially other fields) and sends them via HTTP(S) POST to an attacker-controlled endpoint, often using XMLHttpRequest or fetch(). The overlay is designed to be indistinguishable from the real login page, tricking users into submitting their credentials.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user attempts to log in on the fake overlay, the JavaScript captures the entered credentials from the form fields, transmits them via HTTP(S) POST to an attacker-controlled server, and prevents legitimate authentication, resulting in credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is engineered to deceive users by presenting a visually identical login page overlay, capturing sensitive credentials, and exfiltrating them to an unauthorized external server controlled by the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Users expect to interact with the authentic loyalty program login page, where credentials are securely transmitted to the legitimate service provider, not intercepted and sent to unknown third parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate login pages collect user credentials for authentication but never transmit them to domains outside the official service. Any credential collection that posts to non-canonical domains is highly suspicious.
key_indicators: Presence of a login page overlay that closely mimics the legitimate site
JavaScript capturing form field values and sending them to external, non-canonical domains
Network requests (POST) to attacker-controlled endpoints upon form submission
Overlay hosted on domains similar to, but not exactly matching, the legitimate loyalty program

execution_context.trigger: On page load or user interaction within the legitimate loyalty program page
execution_context.file_location: Injected or embedded JavaScript within the actual loyalty program page source (via supply chain compromise, XSS, or unauthorized script inclusion)
required_permissions: access to DOM elements and user input fields
read access to cookies and local storage

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious JavaScript code injected into the legitimate loyalty program page. The script reads sensitive user data from form fields (such as contact information, payment card details, and user preferences), accesses cookies or local storage for session tokens, and transmits this data via HTTP(S) POST or WebSocket to an attacker-controlled server. The code may use obfuscation or dynamic script loading to evade detection.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On page load or user interaction, the injected JavaScript accesses sensitive user data from form fields, cookies, or local storage, then transmits this information via HTTP(S) POST to an attacker-controlled endpoint, resulting in unauthorized data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script surreptitiously collects sensitive user data—including credentials, contact details, and payment information—from the legitimate loyalty program page and exfiltrates it to an external server without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate loyalty program pages should only transmit user data to trusted, official domains and never send sensitive information to unrecognized or unauthorized third parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Analytics or customer support scripts may collect limited, non-sensitive data for legitimate business purposes, but should never access or transmit full credentials, payment details, or session tokens to external domains.
key_indicators: Injected or unauthorized JavaScript present in the page source
Script accessing sensitive form fields, cookies, or local storage
Outbound HTTP(S) requests or WebSocket connections to unrecognized or attacker-controlled domains
Obfuscated or dynamically loaded JavaScript code not present in the official codebase

attack_chain.action: User is lured to a fake loyalty program login page (transparent overlay) or visits a legitimate loyalty program page that has been compromised with injected malicious JavaScript.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential or sensitive data capture by attacker

attack_chain.action: Malicious code captures user credentials or sensitive data (such as contact information and payment details) and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled infrastructure via outbound network requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to loyalty accounts and personal information

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages stolen credentials and data for account takeover, fraudulent transactions, or resale of information on underground markets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Financial loss, privacy breach, and reputational damage for both customers and the affected business

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network requests from loyalty program pages to unrecognized or non-canonical domains
Credential or sensitive data capture on login pages not hosted on official domains
JavaScript accessing and transmitting form data, cookies, or local storage contents externally
Presence of overlays or pop-ups that mimic legitimate login interfaces
file_indicators: Injected or unauthorized JavaScript code present in the loyalty program page source (e.g., script tags referencing unknown domains or inline scripts not in the official codebase)
Lookalike login pages hosted on domains that closely resemble, but do not exactly match, the legitimate loyalty program domain
Obfuscated or dynamically loaded scripts not present in the official deployment
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing credentials or PII to attacker-controlled or untrusted domains
Network traffic to domains or IPs not associated with the legitimate loyalty program infrastructure
Unusual WebSocket connections initiated from loyalty program pages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor loyalty program pages for unauthorized JavaScript inclusions, overlays, or DOM modifications. Scan for outbound network requests to unrecognized or non-canonical domains, especially those transmitting credentials or PII. Audit for the presence of lookalike login pages on similar domains. Employ automated journey scans with varied user profiles to detect data leakage or exfiltration attempts, and compare deployed code against known-good baselines to identify unauthorized changes.
